training_lineage.checkpoint_to_export_audit_scope: Existing strict export-audit receipts and full checkpoint bytes verified. This independent native review recomputes C++ output parity against the saved JSON networks; it does not deserialize training checkpoints or rerun Torch export.

directional_tradeoffs.scope: Descriptive comparisons include stage transients; mean-error and RMSE definitions remain distinct. No aggregate ranking or new pass threshold.

verdict.conclusion: Both nominal chains finish with quiet default stopping and zero sampled torso load during the three walking commands. The measured-sensing-trained actor reduces equal-stage mean moving torso support in all four selected donor/material pairs but retains support and directional tracking/slip tradeoffs. All eight donor-case default tails fail the original 2 s and extended 8 s quiet screens. No installed-policy or hardware-success conclusion follows from clock completion or the support reduction.

limitations: One training seed and two startup worlds selected posthoc, each under two material assumptions; this is a bounded paired diagnostic, not a reliability estimate.

Both arms use measured q+b in native deployment; nominal bias zero makes sensing conventions numerically equal. Export encoder metadata describes training and is not used to force legacy sensing during this native comparison.

Only walking network weights and training-contract metadata differ within each pair. The fixed entry/exit and default policies, compiled model and pre-walking history are identical; the later realized state can differ because the walking networks differ.
Both native and training settings differ: native full hull geometry at 520 Hz, training torso hull at 250 Hz; no stochastic sensor noise/IMU delay/reset transfer in native runs.

Tracking RMSE includes stage transients and uses requested constant body XY / world yaw commands. Effective yaw heading assistance is reported separately; worldheading rate is not body-frame angular velocity. No posthoc tracking pass threshold imposed.

Torso load and force-weighted tangential contact speed are verified from recorded 52 Hz contact forces/velocities; relative velocity projection verified for every contact. Contact positions, forces and velocities share prestep copied/forward-solved state. Stored root/joint states are after one 520 Hz step. No unrecorded continuous contact claims.

No physics stepping was performed; absolute contact Jacobians/forces cannot be fully independently reconstructed from 52 Hz poststep records. Their collection algorithm was inspected in the pinned source.

Quiet uses every selected last 0.5 s sample below .02 m/s body planar speed, .05 rad/s unwrapped-worldheading difference and each joint below .05 rad/s; 26 states span 25/52 s. Independent worldXY interval speeds produce the same verdict. 2 s and 8 s windows remain separate.
The fixed default controller has a separately established adverse mass/inertia robustness failure; its failure is not evidence that this walking-actor change alone caused or fixed it.

All target clamps, sampled 3 Nm torque cap and 15 rad/s walking-target slew checks pass; physical soft joint-range excursions are separately quantified. Neither implies measured hardware limits or safety.
No robot, deployment, candidate installation, or training was performed by this audit.
